description:
I am an EEE student interested in space, science, technology, and creative problem-solving. I enjoy learning new things, exploring ideas, and taking on challenges. I am excited to participate in NASA Space Apps Challenge and develop my skills through research, creativity, and independent work. I am a beginner, but I am dedicated, curious, and willing to learn.

I will be participating as a solo participant.
summary: Abandoned but Not Forgotten is a storytelling-based educational project about the equipment NASA left behind on the Moon and Mars. It covers the Apollo Lunar Module descent stages, the Lunar Roving Vehicles and scientific instruments on the Moon, and the Perseverance landing hardware on Mars (heat shield, parachute, backshell and descent stage). The project explains why equipment is left behind, compares the Moon and Mars, and gives simple first-person stories for objects like the rover, heat shield and descent stage to make the topic easy to connect with. It matters because these objects are not waste: they are evidence of engineering achievement and the history of exploration. The project also suggests ways to protect this space heritage, such as recording locations, studying landing sites through satellite images and avoiding unnecessary disturbance.
details: The project uses a simple storytelling approach to explain space heritage. Across seven slides, it explains why missions leave equipment behind (limited storage, weight, landing-only parts, instruments designed to stay), shows what remains on the Moon (Apollo descent stages, Lunar Roving Vehicles, scientific instruments) and on Mars (Perseverance heat shield, parachute, backshell, descent stage), and walks through the Perseverance landing sequence. A Moon vs Mars comparison and three short first-person stories, clearly labelled as creative interpretations and not real statements, make the topic engaging. The project ends by explaining why these objects matter and how space heritage can be protected. Tools: presentation slides (PowerPoint format) with simple shapes and diagrams. The text, slide layout and file were created with the help of an AI assistant (Claude). Intended impact: to help students and the public appreciate space history and respect historic sites.
